# Arjun Mehta — CV

## Education
- M.Tech, Robotics, Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru, 2025–2027 (expected). CGPA 9.4/10.
- B.E., Mechanical Engineering, BITS Pilani, 2020–2024. CGPA 8.9/10.

## Research experience
- **Research assistant, Robot Learning Lab, IISc** (Aug 2025 – present), advised by Prof. Meera Natarajan.
  Built a diffusion-policy pipeline for a $1,800 6-DoF arm; with 40 teleoperated demonstrations per task the
  policy reached 78% success on cup stacking and 61% on towel folding, versus 44% / 29% for a behaviour-cloning
  baseline. Submitted to a robotics conference workshop (under review).
- **Summer intern, TCS Research, Bengaluru** (May–July 2025), mentor: Dr. Ravi Shankar.
  Real-to-sim reconstruction of a kitchen counter from 12 phone photos; policies trained in the reconstructed
  scene transferred to the real counter with a 17-point drop in success instead of 41 points for a generic
  simulated scene.
- **Undergraduate project, BITS Pilani (2023–24):** low-cost tactile skin (piezoresistive fabric, 64 taxels)
  for a parallel gripper; detected slip within 60 ms in 91% of trials.

## Publications
- A. Mehta, S. Rao, M. Natarajan. "Few-Shot Diffusion Policies on a Sub-$2k Arm." Robotics workshop paper, 2026 (under review, first author).
- A. Mehta, P. Iyer. "A 64-Taxel Fabric Tactile Skin for Slip Detection." Undergraduate research symposium, BITS Pilani, 2024.

## Skills
- Python, PyTorch, ROS 2, Isaac Sim, MuJoCo, OpenCV; C++ for real-time control; 3D printing and basic electronics.

## Awards
- Institute Gold Medal, Mechanical Engineering, BITS Pilani, 2024.
- Best demo, IISc Robotics Day 2026.

## Service
- Teaching assistant, Introduction to Robotics (M.Tech core), Spring 2026, 60 students.

items.text:
# Research interests

I want to work on robot learning for manipulation in unstructured homes, specifically:

1. Learning from few demonstrations: diffusion policies and visuomotor imitation that generalise across object
   instances and lighting, with a focus on cheap hardware (sub-$2,000 arms).
2. Tactile sensing for deformable objects (cloth, food), combining vision with low-cost tactile skins.
3. Sim-to-real for household tasks: domain randomisation and real-to-sim scene reconstruction so that policies
   trained in simulation transfer to a real kitchen.

Secondary: assistive robotics for elderly care in Indian households; safety constraints for learned policies.

items.text:
# Statement of purpose — rough draft

I want to build robots that can help in ordinary homes, which means learning manipulation skills from very
little data on hardware that families can afford. My M.Tech work at IISc has been about exactly that gap: with
40 demonstrations per task, a diffusion policy on a $1,800 arm reached 78% on cup stacking and 61% on towel
folding, far above a behaviour-cloning baseline. The towel number is the one I think about most: deformable
objects are where vision alone fails, and where my undergraduate tactile skin (64 taxels, slip detected in 60 ms)
suggests a cheap way forward.

At TCS Research I worked on the other half of the problem, getting simulation to look like a real kitchen:
reconstructing a counter from twelve phone photos cut the sim-to-real success drop from 41 points to 17.

In a PhD I want to combine these threads: few-shot visuomotor learning, low-cost tactile sensing for deformable
objects, and real-to-sim transfer for household tasks, with assistive robotics for elderly care as the setting
that matters most to me.
